result.title: Same Executions, Different Gaps: Judgment Rules in Web-Agent Evaluation
result.summary: Success-rate gains guide the development of web agents. Yet knowing which agent ranks first does not tell us how much confidence to place in its reported advantage. We study the comparison itself: how success is defined, what evidence supports the judgments, and how the difference between agents is estimated. On fixed web-agent executions, changing a judge from predicting likely completion to requiring recorded support can remove most of a reported lead without changing the ranking. This effect persists when unresolved completion is distinguished from supported failure. Controlled source additions explain how missing relations between task requirements, objects and observations can conceal a difference or create an apparent advantage. We also find that making both agents' score estimates more accurate can make their difference less accurate, because their original errors partly canceled. To estimate a chosen outcome difference, we combine judge predictions with reference labels for sampled task pairs. Across four released execution systems, regression fitted on the same 50 labeled pairs reduces estimation error relative to direct paired sampling. The results give agent researchers a practical basis for assessing claimed improvements: make the comparison target explicit, retain the evidence needed to check it, and use paired labels to estimate the difference directly.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 web agent 评测的比较过程本身作为研究对象：成功如何定义、判断依据何种证据、agent 间差异如何估计；发现将评判从「预测可能完成」改为「要求记录支持」可在不改变排名的情况下消除大部分报告优势，并提出用评判预测结合抽样任务对的参考标签来直接估计差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对「评判规则—证据要求—差异估计」的拆解可能可供核查 LVR 方法增益报告中由评测口径与证据缺失带来的虚假优势，属评价层面的启发，但不涉及多模态内部状态或 latent 生成本身。
